dicas.texto: Você está indo bem! O que significa ter 33 partes de 12? Quantos grupos completos de 12 cabem dentro de 33?
Tente dividir 33 por 12. Quantas vezes o 12 cabe no 33 sem passar dele? Esse será seu número inteiro (m1).
Se 12 x 2 = 24, quanto sobra de 33 para chegar em 24? Essa sobra é o seu novo numerador (m2).
Você tem 2 inteiros (24/12). Para chegar em 33/12, falta quanto? O denominador (m3) continua sendo o mesmo da fração original (12).

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem?" com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); reta numérica de 0 a 3 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 12 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

dicas.texto: The numerator tells how many parts or objects are being counted.
Look at the number above the fraction bar.
Use the number that represents Katie's total collection of pens.
Type the total number of pens into the top fraction box.
The denominator tells how many equal items make one whole unit.
Look at the number below the fraction bar.
One dozen always contains the same number of pens.
Enter the number of pens in one dozen into the bottom fraction box.
A whole number represents complete units, not just part of a unit.
Find zero first, then move one whole unit to the right.
The point is at the first whole-number mark after zero.
Place the point exactly on the first integer mark to the right of zero.
An improper fraction can show complete units together with a remaining fractional part.
Use the whole-number part from dividing the numerator by the denominator, then keep the remainder over the same denominator.
Thirty-three contains two complete groups of twelve, with some pens left over.
Click Convert so the interface can display the whole-number part and the remaining fraction.
A mixed number combines complete units with a fractional part.
Start at the whole-number part, then move through the fraction of the next unit.
Begin at 2 and move nine of the twelve equal intervals toward 3.
Count nine equal subdivisions to the right of 2 and place the point at that location.
Before finishing, make sure the point represents the complete mixed number, not only its fractional part.
Check that the point is between 2 and 3 and that it is divided into twelve equal intervals.
The point should be nine intervals after 2.
Verify the point, then click Done to submit the completed number-line representation.

nodes.description: Inversão por viés de que o denominador é sempre o maior número.
nodes.instruction: You entered the denominator as the numerator. Check the order in 33/12: the numerator is the total number of pens, while 12 defines one dozen.

nodes.description: Aluno marca apenas a parte fracionária, ignorando o inteiro (2) na reta numérica.
nodes.instruction: You used only the fractional part and ignored the two complete dozens. The point must be located two whole units to the right of zero before adding the remaining fraction.

nodes.description: Erro de contagem: contar as linhas em vez dos espaços entre elas.
nodes.instruction: You counted the marks instead of the intervals between them. Count nine of the twelve equal spaces after 2.

nodes.description: O aluno foca no que falta para completar a próxima unidade (3/12) em vez da fração (9/12).
nodes.instruction: You marked the amount needed to reach the next whole number instead of the fraction already present. Locate nine twelfths after 2.
